title: Native Heap 分配器：jemalloc、Scudo 与 malloc 调试
key_conclusions: Native Heap growth must be diagnosed through allocator behavior, mappings, and allocation stacks rather than as a Java-style object graph.
Leak, fragmentation, cache retention, and allocator-retained pages can all look like Native Heap or PSS growth, so they need separate evidence.
dumpsys meminfo provides the Native Heap bucket, showmap/smaps explain mappings, and heapprofd or malloc_debug provides native allocation call stacks.
Scudo, jemalloc, malloc_debug, and heapprofd have different goals and overheads; target Android version, build type, and configuration must be validated before relying on exact output.
shallow_points: The article does not include real heapprofd or malloc_debug traces from a target device.
It does not validate exact jemalloc versus Scudo defaults across Android versions, process types, or vendor builds.
It does not include a runnable native leak, fragmentation, cache, and DirectByteBuffer sample app.
It does not provide a parser that joins Native Heap bucket deltas, showmap rows, smaps_rollup, and heapprofd stack totals.

Day 27's PSS/RSS/USS boundaries still matter because native RSS growth can be shared or privately retained.
